topic: Could we live in a fossil-fuel-free world?
research_question: Under what combinations of renewable and other low-carbon generation, electrification, storage, transmission, demand flexibility, sustainable fuels, efficiency, and non-fossil feedstocks can a region eliminate fossil-fuel extraction and combustion while satisfying hourly reliability, energy-service, affordability, access, lifecycle-emissions, land, water, mineral, and governance constraints?

candidate_routes.name: electrification_first
candidate_routes.reason: reduces combustion and conversion losses where electricity can preserve the required service

candidate_routes.name: renewable_plus_flexibility
candidate_routes.reason: tests wind and solar with transmission, storage, overbuild, and demand response under correlated weather stress

candidate_routes.name: firm_and_seasonal_supply
candidate_routes.reason: addresses multi-day and seasonal adequacy with explicit resource and safety constraints

candidate_routes.name: industrial_molecules_and_feedstocks
candidate_routes.reason: addresses aviation, shipping, steel, chemicals, and non-energy carbon needs

candidate_routes.name: demand_reduction_and_sufficiency
candidate_routes.reason: reduces infrastructure requirements while preserving energy services and testing equity

candidate_routes.name: coordinated_transition_portfolio
candidate_routes.reason: integrates technical portfolios with networks, manufacturing, policy, affordability, and adoption lead times

falsifiable_claims: annual balance overstates feasibility under correlated stress
electrification and flexibility reduce fossil backup at matched service reliability
clean electricity does not establish full fossil independence
lifecycle and infrastructure constraints can reorder technology choices
required_boundaries: distinguish fossil-free from net-zero with CCS
model delivered services rather than primary fuel
include distributional outcomes and transition lead times
